CITY OF SAN MARINO

  CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

Steve Talt, Mayor  www.CityofSanMarino.org

Steven W. Huang, DDS, Vice Mayor  (626) 300-0700 Phone

Calvin Lo, Council Member  2200 Huntington Drive

Gretchen Shepherd Romey, Council Member  San Marino, CA 91108

Philippe Eskandar, City Manager

  REGULAR MEETING OF THE
  SAN MARINO CITY COUNCIL
  WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 13, 2023 AT 6:00 PM
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  2200 HUNTINGTON DRIVE
  SAN MARINO, CA 91108
  AND
  326 FRONT STREET
  KETCHIKAN, AK 99902

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Council
with  valuable  information  regarding  issues  of  the  community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Wednesday of every month at 6:00 p.m. Typically,
adjourned  meetings are held  on  the last  Friday of every month  at  8:30  a.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the City Clerk via email at CityClerk@CityofSanMarino.org or by phone at
(626)  300-0705  prior  to  the  meeting  for  assistance.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City
will  do  its  best  to  resolve  any  technical  issues  as  quickly  as  possible.

How to view or listen to the meeting from home:
  Via Computer for Video Streaming:
  Website: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/83316497270
  Meeting ID: 833 1649 7270

   Via Phone for Audio Only:
  Phone Number: (669) 900-9128
  Meeting ID: 833 1649 7270

How to offer public comment from home:

  Public comment will be accepted by email to CityClerk@CityofSanMarino.org until
  3:00 p.m. the day of the meeting, to be read by the City Clerk during public
  comment. Lengthy public comment may be summarized in the interest of time, and
  previously distributed public comment will be noted. Any comments received after
  3:00 p.m. will be included in the public comment record but will not be read at the
  meeting.
  Public comment will be accepted electronically via the zoom.us teleconference
  module during the meeting. Zoom comments will be taken after the in-person
  comments.

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL

Council Member Chou, Council Member Lo, Council Member Shepherd Romey, Vice Mayor
Huang, and Mayor Talt

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the
Stoneman Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the City Council by
completing a public comment card and giving it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. At
this time, the public may address the City Council on items that are not on the agenda.
Pursuant to state law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on issues not on the
meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The Mayor reserves the right to
place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to follow up on such items.

CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

This is an opportunity for the City Manager to inform the City Council and the public of any
upcoming events or matters of interest to the community.

AGENDA – SEPTEMBER 13, 2023  PAGE 2 of 5
 MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READINGS

This action permits the City Council to act on ordinances and resolutions without having to
read the entire text of the ordinance or resolution. The title of an ordinance on First
Reading must be read in its entirety. An ordinance on Second Reading does not require
having the title read. However, the City Council may request that an ordinance or
resolution be read in its entirety before taking any action.

  CEREMONIAL

 RECOGNITION OF THE 2023 CITY OF SAN MARINO PHOTO CONTEST
 WINNERS

  NEW BUSINESS

 1.  ADOPTION OF AN URGENCY ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING A
  TEMPORARY MORATORIUM ON THE INSTALLATION OF ARTIFICIAL
  TURF AND SYNTHETIC GRASS IN THE CITY OF SAN MARINO

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council adopt Urgency Ordinance No.
  O-21-1385-U, by a four-fifths vote and then direct staff to notice a public hearing on
  a possible extension of the Ordinance. If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation,  an  appropriate  motion  would  be:

  “I move to adopt Urgency Ordinance No. O-21-1385-U, an Urgency Ordinance of the
  City Council of San Marino, California, establishing a temporary moratorium on the
  installation of artificial turf and synthetic grass to allow staff time to research and
  develop artificial turf and synthetic grass regulations that will be presented to Council
  for consideration and potential adoption and further direct staff to notice a public
  hearing for the Council to consider a possible extension to such Ordinance.

 2.  APPROVAL OF AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 1 WITH DUDEK FOR
  PROFESSIONAL DESIGN SERVICES FOR THE CULVERT REPLACEMENT
  PROGRAM IN THE AMOUNT OF $80,400 AND EXTENDING THE TERM
  THROUGH DECEMBER 31, 2024, AND AUTHORIZE APPROPRIATION OF
  $80,400  FROM  CAPITAL  IMPROVEMENT  FUND  RESERVES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve Amendment No. 1
  with Dudek increasing the compensation amount by $80,400 and extending the term
  of the Professional Design Services Agreement through December 31, 2024, and
  authorize the appropriation of $80,400 into Account # 394-46-4600-8024 (Culvert
  Replacement Program) from the CIP reserves. If the City Council concurs with staff’s
  recommendation,  an  appropriate  motion  would  be:

  “I move to approve Amendment No. 1 with Dudek for the Culvert Replacement
  Program Project No. 21-8024 increasing the compensation amount by $80,400 and
  extending the term of the Professional Design Services Agreement through December

AGENDA – SEPTEMBER 13, 2023  PAGE 3 of 5
   31, 2024, and authorize the appropriation of $80,400 into Account # 394-46-4600-
  8024 (Culvert Replacement Program) from the CIP reserves, and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the amendment on behalf of the City.”

  CONSENT CALENDAR

 3.  FALL 2023 PUBLIC TREE REMOVAL LIST

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council approve the attached tree
  removal list. If the City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate
  motion  would  be:

  “I move to approve the Fall 2023 recommended tree removal list.”

 4.  APPROVAL TO PURCHASE SIMUNITION TRAINING FIREARMS AND
  AMMUNITION THROUGH THE USE OF COPS FUND RESERVES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the City Council authorize the purchase of
  Simunition firearms, associated ammunition and support equipment and approve a
  budget amendment and appropriation of $9,931 from the COPS Fund reserves to
  account 233-30-4613-0000 (Capitalized Equipment). If the Council concurs with
  staff’s  recommendation,  an  appropriate  motion  would  be:

  “I move to authorize the purchase of Simunition firearms, associated ammunition and
  support equipment and approve a budget amendment and appropriation of $9,931
  from the COPS Fund reserves to account 233-30-4613-0000 (Capitalized
  Equipment).”

 5.  CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT FOR THE MONTH OF JUNE 2023

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Cash and Investment Report for the Month of June
  2023.”

 6.  CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT FOR THE MONTH OF JULY 2023

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file this report. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to receive and file the Cash and Investment Report for the Month of July
  2023.”

 7.  RECEIVE AND FILE MONTHLY DISBURSEMENTS REPORT FOR JULY
  2023

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file the Monthly

   Disbursements Report for the month of July 2023. If the City Council concurs with
  staff’s  recommendation,  an  appropriate  motion  would  be:

  “I move to receive and file the Monthly Disbursements Report for the month of July
  2023.”

8.  RECEIVE AND FILE MONTHLY DISBURSEMENTS REPORT FOR AUGUST
  2023

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council receive and file the Monthly
  Disbursements Report for the month of August 2023. If the City Council concurs with
  staff’s  recommendation,  an  appropriate  motion  would  be:

  “I move to receive and file the Monthly Disbursements Report for the month of August
  2023.”

9.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Recommendation: Staff recommends the Council approve the July 2023 minutes. If the
  City Council concurs with staff’s recommendation, an appropriate motion would be:

  “I move to approve the minutes of the regular meeting of July 12, 2023, and the
  adjourned regular meeting of July 28, 2023.”

WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS OR PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTION

This is an opportunity to announce any written communications pertaining to the City
received by members of the City Council. All public writings distributed by the City of San
Marino to at least a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be
made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San
Marino, California 91108, and will also be included in the public agenda packet that will
available for review at the City Council meeting.
